question.text: Which element has the highest electronegativity?

hints: Consider the general trend of electronegativity across the periodic table.
Electronegativity generally increases as you move across a period and up a group.
The element is found in Group 17 (halogens) and Period 2.
explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element, meaning it has the strongest tendency to attract electrons in a chemical bond. This property makes it highly reactive and explains its strong oxidizing power.
